findings.claim: Enum formatters use the inverse target-framework condition from every other template. Consequently, on modern targets such as net8.0 the enum formatter's ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute is inactive, so not all generated code is decorated. On NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK it is instead active even though the change identifies those as targets where the attribute is unavailable, breaking the supported-target compilation criterion there.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.EnumExcludeFromCodeCoverageRequirementTests.EnumFormatter_HasActiveExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttributeOnModernTargets. It parses the generated enum formatter with modern-target preprocessor symbols and fails on head because the attribute occurs only inside inactive '#if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK' text. Additionally, compiling that generated formatter with NETSTANDARD2_0 against netstandard2.0 references exercises the reversed availability branch.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decorate every generated type without adding a setting: object/string-key, enum, and union formatters, resolver classes, and nested resolver formatter-cache/helper classes, suppressing the attribute only through target-availability preprocessor guards. This is the scope the change attempts to implement.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Interpret the coverage request as covering generated formatter classes only, still unconditionally where the attribute exists; omit it from resolvers and their nested helper classes by removing the ResolverTemplate and CompositeResolverTemplate additions while retaining the formatter-template additions.
